does: Grates a daikon on a fine grater into a wet, light, snowy mound, which is eaten raw beside rich or grilled food to freshen the mouth.
how: Peel the daikon, or leave the skin on if it is tender, and cut it into a piece that is easy to hold.
Grate it with firm, even strokes on the finest side of the grater, in one direction.
Let the juice drain away a little in a sieve, but do not press it dry.
Shape the mound with a spoon and serve it straight away.

cues.text: The grated daikon is a soft, wet, white mound.
The taste is fresh, juicy and a little sharp.

mistakes.mistake: Grating long ahead, so that it turns bitter and watery.
Squeezing it dry, which leaves it harsh.

variant_of.differs: It is grated very fine and wet, kept juicy and loose and served as a raw mound, not dried or used to flavour a dish.
